My read: this is a small- to mid-market logo but a good strategic reference in vertical (SaaS infra) and they want a fast turnaround. The ask (60% rev-share + Net30 + $120k 6mo commit) is outside standard marketplace guardrails. If we want to close quickly, I recommend a compromise: 45% rev-share for first 12 months, Net30 billing, and front-loaded 6-month $100k commit (they asked for $120k) with a carveout that rev-share steps down back to standard on renewal. This preserves unit economics and keeps the customer happy.

Can you take a quick margin + policy view, @Karthik? @Marissa — need exec signoff to proceed with legal drafting/DocuSign. Priyom looping for indemnity/WC language.

Thanks,

Sofia / Marissa —

Thanks for the note and the suggested compromise. Quick financials:
- Baseline: our standard marketplace rev-share to partners is 30%. At 60% we'd be negative margin on first-year net unit economics for this deal unless we push higher commit dollars.
- Impact of Sofia's proposal (45% rev-share, $100k 6mo commit): estimated first 12-month revenue to Redwood ~ $55k net -> gross margin around 18% after infra and marketplace fees, which is tight but acceptable if Nimbus becomes a strategic reference.

Risks/asks: legal needs to sign off on the rev-share carveout language (term cap, audit rights), and finance needs to approve Net30 cash flow impact. If execs approve, I recommend we make the rev-share time-limited (12 months), require the $100k consumed-commit to be tracked in HubSpot (deal RDW-2028-0439), and include a market-fee pass-through clause so we aren't absorbing AWS listing fees.

If we want to push back and preserve margin, alternate offer: keep standard rev-share (30%) and require $150k commit. Given their ask and speed requirement, Sofia's compromise seems the fastest path to close.
